- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) in recent days, reduce forecasted price spikes; model tends to overreact.
- If model shows a sharp upward spike followed by a forecasted drop, check for mean reversion bias — often overcorrects downward.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is rising, model may overestimate continuation — cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak.
- If last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum (e.g., 3 consecutive drops), model often underestimates rebound — add 5–10% upward bias for next 3–5 days.
- If forecast is consistently 5–10% above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply downward adjustment — model tends to overestimate bullish sentiment.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.7), model often averages out — use weighted average of recent 7-day mean + sentiment trend.
- If sentiment is flat or near 0.5, model tends to forecast mean-reversion — align with 20-day moving average of price history.
- If forecast shows a large upward move after a low sentiment day, reduce by 10–20% — sentiment often suppresses momentum.
